Be The Best You Can Be
John Scurr Primary School
John Scurr Primary School honours the values of John and Julia Scurr who fought for equality and access to education for East End families 90 years ago. We offer an inclusive and enriched curriculum to develop all aspects of learning for children.
We have a dedicated and skilled workforce, who work hard with our governors and parents to promote good progress and attainment for all, and we have high expectations of everyone in our school and value their contribution.

pageCache.pageTitle: Home School Partnership - John Scurr Primary School
pageCache.text:
Home School Partnership
Homework
At John Scurr we call homework “home learning.” It is used to enable children to remember, practise and apply what they have been learning. We provide home learning that concentrates on English and Maths skills. This is given on Friday and must be completed by Wednesday. Children in KS2, who do not complete home learning, attend lunchtime Catch up Club. Children, who need support with their home learning are provided with this at an after school club.
We expect every child to read for 10 minutes every day (in EYFS/KS1) and 20 minutes at KS2.- Phonic Bug and Accelerated Reader programmes are checked weekly to ensure that the children are reading at home to work towards the class Reading Pledge.
Children in KS1 have homework books and are given weekly homework related to their English and Maths learning. Children in KS2 are given home learning from the published English and Maths books they are provided with by the school. In addition to this, they are expected to complete specific online activities: Phonics Bug, Spellodrome, Mathletics and Times Tables Rockstars.
In addition, each term the children are given the opportunity to develop their learning through extended activities for English, Maths, Science and the Wider Curriculum. These projects provide a range of challenges for children to complete at home with support from parents. The main focus will be on creating and making. We celebrate this in our Homework Hero Assembly.
Our Family Support Worker and Achievement Advocate stronger support families who struggle to provide support at home through signposting services and the local library.

pageCache.text:
Clubs & Wrap-around Care
There are many options to support the extended day for pupils John Scurr
Tea Time Club (TTC) from 3:15 – 4:00- this allows support and care for children whose parents are studying or working and need some extra time at the end of the day. This session costs £1.
After School Club (ASC) – Wednesday 3:15 – 4:00 Lead by support staff for all year groups from Reception and above. Please see Rebecca O’ Brien or Satnam Sokhal for more information. This session costs £5 for the whole term.
Bethnal Green ASC – if any parent needs an extended school day (beyond 4pm) their child can enrol at this scheme supported by a collaboration with 4 other local primary schools. Children are collected form the school for a later finish at 6pm
Bethnal Green ASC Website
Breakfast Club: 8:00 – 8:45 From Reception – Y6 this is a free service for parents that need support in providing breakfast at the start of the school day and is also suitable for children who are not reading or accessing online learning platforms at home
Ambassador Programmes (New for 24/25) – these are programmes that run after school to support pupil’s skills and talents in Sport, Technology, Debating and Chess – these are free programmes and usually run after school once a week and lead to participation in National Competitions. Your child’s teacher can give you more information and may approach you to encourage your child onto these programmes.

French
Our Curriculum Drivers are to promote resilience, develop communication and ensure all pupils have access to all learning possibilities both in and out of the classroom.
Intent
Our Curriculum Intent is for pupils to know more, do more and learn more. At John Scurr Primary School, we believe that learning a modern foreign language supports our children to understand and appreciate the diversity in their own country and in the wider world. We intend that our children will learn to express themselves in French and understand the responses of their audience. They will appreciate the similarities and differences between French and English and develop the linguistic fluency to help them find their place as a global citizen.
Early Years and Key Stage 1
It is not statutory for Early Years, Year 1 and Year 2 to learn a modern foreign language. However, the children in these phases will begin to develop an interest in French language and culture by participating in whole school events like French Language and Culture Day. They may also learn simple French songs as part of the classroom singing practice.
Key Stage 2
It is statutory for all children in Key Stage 2 to learn a modern foreign language. At John Scurr all children in Key Stage 2 have a scheduled weekly French lesson based on the Cusp Curriculum.
What Do We Teach
Block A Greetings and the classroom.
Block B Numbers, Colours and Emotions
Block C Introductions and Questions

Block F Visiting France
Links To Other Learning
Cusp French lessons make regular connections to Geography so that the children develop a good understanding of the geographical position of France, its neighbours and other French speaking countries. Particular features of French history are taught to compare French and British systems of government. Cusp lessons also develop the children’s understanding of French culture and customs, including a focus on architecture, food and religious customs. The children also learn to appreciate traditional French songs, poems and rhymes.
How Do Pupils Learn
French is currently taught in 30 min weekly sessions, in each KS2 Class at John Scurr, with additional 5 min bursts of retrieval practice through the week. Cusp Curriculum French lessons primarily focus on vocabulary, phonics, oracy and reading and writing French. They follow the familiar lesson structure of CEEAAC: Connect, Explain, Example, Attempt, Apply, Challenge, which is used across the Cusp curriculum. As in other foundation curriculum subjects, knowledge organisers and knowledge notes are used to support the children’s retrieval of French vocabulary over time.
The French curriculum allows children to develop their ability to listen to French phrases and pronounce them, to read and write French, to gain an understanding of French grammar and finally to develop intercultural understanding through the exploration of wider French culture.
French lessons allow children the opportunity to retrieve and revise previous learning regularly and to develop their knowledge of new French vocabulary. Children are encouraged to participate in mostly verbal activities to listen to and refine French pronunciation. They enjoy participating in games and oral discussion to improve their pronunciation. They will also record their ideas when creating grammatical sentences in French.
How Do We Know What Pupils Have Learned?
Questioning
Retrieval practice
Oral Feedback
Talking to teachers
Low stakes ‘Drop-in’ observations
How Does The Curriculum Progress?
Progression within the French curriculum allows children to build on a growing bank of French vocabulary and phrases. They develop their confidence in engaging in conversations, in asking and answering questions and in expressing opinions and responding to those of others. The children develop an understanding of the differences and similarities between the English and French languages and cultures.

Governors
The John Scurr Governing Body is a board of members who represent different parts of the school community and who all bring different skills to the task of leading our school onwards.
Staff Governors: One of whom is the Headteacher. The other staff governor is elected by the school staff team. Staff governors represent the views of staff at John Scurr at governing body meetings.
Co-opted Governors: Are appointed by the governing body to represent the skills needed to Govern the school. These governors are selected for the skills they bring to the Governing Body.
A Local Authority (LA) Governor: Is appointed by the LA which maintains the school. They are people who live or work locally and are interested in supporting a local school.
Parent Governors: Are voted onto the governing body by other parents of children who attend the school. Parent governors play an important role in shaping the education and experience of their children at John Scurr.
Associate Governors: Are invited to Governors meetings and are informed about school life. They help provide the strategy and information for continual improvement but do not have voting rights.
Kevin Hinde
Chair of Curriculum and Standards, Safeguarding and Health and Safety Lead
I became a governor at John Scurr Primary School in 2008 and I have been Chair of Governors since 2018.
I was born in Crewe, Cheshire and moved to London in 1995 for work after university. My work is in management, technology and publishing. I have a lifelong interest in the power of education, in particular through science and literature. My three children attended John Scurr, they have now progressed to secondary school and beyond. The school made an immediate impression on me as a happy, welcoming place where the staff really care about all of the children.
Being a School Governor is a wonderful way to contribute to the local community, with many opportunities to learn and grow while supporting a school – making a genuine impact on children’s education. In my spare time I enjoy running, swimming and cycling, and I read and go to the cinema and the theatre as often as I am able to.
Nicola Denton-Dash
Xina Li
I became a governor at John Scurr Primary School in 2019 and I have been Chair of the Finance Committee since 2021.
The industry I work in organise Number/Reading Partner schemes whereby a group of volunteers attend a primary school in Tower Hamlet during lunch hours to help children with their maths and reading skills through either playing maths-based games or reading books with the children. This is how I came to know John Scurr and the reason why I am also the Maths Link Governor as I have a keen interest in mathematics and encouraging children to develop their maths skills through fun and engaging ways of learning.
I have a background in engineering and also in the financial services sector. Being a School Governor means that I can use my financial skills to help challenge the school budget and it is a great way to give something back to the community.
In my spare time, I enjoy dog-walking, running and practicing yoga.
Julie De Young
Finance Committee & Inclusion
My son is in his final year at John Scurr. I’ve seen him flourish from the happiness and safety provided to him. I’m grateful for the considered and comprehensive development he’s experienced over the last seven years.
I became a school governor around three years ago. It’s been interesting to learn the complexities behind running a primary school. I am enjoying my role as a school governor
and happy for the opportunity to support the school in this small way.
My professional life has included a significant amount of time working in the voluntary sector providing support to vulnerable people of all ages. In addition to service provision, my roles included recruitment, training and supervision, as well as working on strategic planning, policies and safeguarding matters. I participated in several management sub-committees during this time and I am very impressed by the range and depth of analysis and information John Scurr provides Governors with, enabling us to ensure that the pupils remain at the centre of all of the schools’ decision-making.
Councillor Srajul Islam
Local Authority Governor
Local Authority Co-opted
I have been a governor of John Scurr School in excess of 20 years. All my children as well as nephews and nieces attended this school. John Scurr is a community school based within the heart of the community. Our parents are made to feel welcome & their children learn in a safe environment.
I am a local resident and moved to the Bancroft Estate in 1985. I am also as a local Labour Councillor & served on the Council for over 20 years.
As a long-standing Governor, I have worked with two previous head teachers and different governing bodies. I have seen the evolution of the school over the past 20 years to the present one under Maria Lewington’s leadership. As governors we are passionate about education & welfare of our children. Most of our children come from a deprived background and live in overcrowded homes. Despite all this our children are excelling in their education attainment. This is thanks to our parents’ commitment & guidance together with the learning provided by our excellent teachers. John Scurr school and its governors are committed to fulfilling the potential of our children.
Joanna Power
Curriculum Committee
My name is Joanne and I have been a Co-opted Governor at John Scurr School since 2014.
I was born and bred in Tower Hamlets where I was lucky enough to receive a first-class education at Cayley primary school and then Raines Foundation Secondary School.
During my school years, I was inspired by some very special teachers who gave me the encouragement to believe in myself and succeed in life.
I became a teacher at John Scurr Primary School in 1990 after completing my PGCE and, since then, have been committed to the school and its community, hoping to inspire the children to achieve their goals just as I had been at their age.
Over the years I have held several roles with increasing responsibility. I am currently an Assistant Head Teacher with responsibility for overseeing Curriculum Development, English, Key Stage 2 and ECTs.
I have enjoyed every minute of my teaching career at John Scurr, watching the school grow from strength to strength. The children are a delight and never cease to amaze me.
My hobbies include reading, gardening and cooking for my family. I enjoy going on holiday after a busy school year to rest, relax and prepare myself for the next one!
Chris McCallum
I joined John Scurr as a Governor in Spring 2025, having started working in Tower Hamlets just over a year prior to that, as the School Business Manager at Morpeth School. I have been a school leader for 6 years now, and alongside my work with John Scurr, I am a governor at two other primary schools in my home Borough of Bexley. I am also treasurer of my children’s primary school PTA.
Kamal Uddin
Curriculum Committee
I have lived in Tower Hamlets for the past 35 years and work in a local GP practice for the past 15 years, where some of my time is spent on clinical work as well as being the IT lead.
‘I have lived in Tower Hamlets for the past 35 years and have been working in a local GP practice for the last 15 years, where some of my time is spent on clinical work as well as being the IT lead and on the Senior Management Team. In addition to this I do Quality Improvement work and help develop training programmes for GP practices across seven boroughs in the Northeast London area.
I am confident that my knowledge of the local area and cultural background, not to mention being a father of 2 adorable daughters, both attending John Scurr, will be beneficial to a school as diverse as John Scurr in representing the parents’ voice.
In my spare time I enjoy learning about most things tech related and love being a father and spending time with my girls, especially trying different restaurants. Ultimately, I would love to enable the children of John Scurr and their families to have access to a safe and fun learning environment where they can flourish and positively contribute to our local communities.’
Hasan Miah
I have lived in Tower Hamlets all my life and feel deeply connected to the community. I completed my entire education up to college within the borough, and now my two children attend John Scurr Primary School, where I proudly serve as a parent governor.
Professionally, I have over a decade of experience in recruitment and operational management within the healthcare and children’s social care sector. I work closely with both the NHS and Children's Social Services, supporting the placement and care of some of the most vulnerable children—particularly those facing mental health challenges and physical disabilities. My background also includes leading teams, overseeing compliance, and operating under pressure to deliver quality outcomes.
I enjoy being a parent governor because I genuinely care about the wellbeing and future of all children—not just my own. It’s a privilege to contribute to a school that plays such an important role in shaping young lives. Supporting the school means supporting the wider community, and I believe every child deserves access to a safe, inspiring, and nurturing learning environment. Being involved allows me to help ensure that children from all backgrounds are given the opportunities, support, and encouragement they need to reach their full potential.
In my spare time, I enjoy family outings, exploring new places and experiences together, and I’m also a keen gamer when time allows.
Nazrul Islam
Co-opted Parent Governor
Curriculum Committee
I’m a family oriented and happily married father of three. I have lived in London, in the same area, since I was 6 months old when my family moved here from Bangladesh. After finishing schools, I went on to support my family business and have been working on it for 10 years.
I am currently working for a charity and based in one of HM Prisons, supporting offenders on their road to rehabilitation and re-joining society. As a part of my professional development, I run peer led groups and coach prison mentors, as well as oversee rehabilitation programs we run in our unit.
As a long-standing member of our community, I believe I have a good understanding of our needs and how to support our children to reach their full potential. I am glad to be part of this vibrant team and have the opportunity to ensure that the school’s vision and mission are in the best interest of our youth.
Nigel Caleb

Our Premium & Sports Strategy
Our Premium Strategy
Pupil Premium Strategy Statement 2025
Our Achievements

Music
Our Music Curriculum
Our Curriculum Drivers : To promote resilience, develop communication and ensure all pupils have access to all learning possibilities both in and out of the classroom.
Intent
Our Curriculum Intent is for pupils to learn more, do more and know more.
What do we teach
Year 1 – Singing and body percussion
Year 3 – African drumming lessons
How do pupils learn
Students develop an understanding of themselves as musicians through listening, playing, analyzing, performing and composing music across a variety of musical styles, periods and genres. Music lessons are spaced out weekly to allow for repetition and retrieval of learning.
Music lessons are supported by Thames Music Specialists and specialist music teachers. Children are also encouraged to consider the different features of the music they are engaging with and how music can express their feelings and emotions.
Students have opportunities to attend performances in school and in wider cultural settings as well as to perform themselves. We also have a mixed-age school choir.
How does the curriculum progress
Progression within the music curriculum allows children to build on their musical experiences and tacit musical knowledge through frequent opportunities to hear, play and perform music. Children build on their skill playing instruments and singing as well as their knowledge of music history, styles and composers.
Links to other learning
Singing, songwriting and composing are linked to learning in other subjects (e.g. Ancient Greek raps, weather songs) where appropriate.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome Message from the Head - John Scurr Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome Message from the Head
John Scurr Primary School honours the values of John and Julia Scurr who fought for equality and access to education for East End families 90 years ago. We offer an IQM accredited inclusive and enriched curriculum with ‘a wide range of outings and extra-curricular activities’ to develop all aspects of learning for children.
We have a dedicated and skilled workforce, who work hard with our governors and parents to promote good progress and attainment for all, and we have high expectations of everyone in our school and value their contribution. Maybe you might be tempted by our parents’ activities or your child may want to be part of our Pupil Voice Committee? We are well hidden amongst our neighbourhood but we are proud to be situated within the heart of the communities that live near Tower Hamlets Town Hall, The Royal London Hospital, Queen Mary University and within the communities of Stepney Green, Bethnal Green and Whitechapel- a real Jewel of the East End!
We are really proud of the curriculum we offer here at John Scurr, where children take full advantage of all that London has to offer. We are a leading school for the knowledge-rich Unity CUSP curriculum – you will be amazed at our ‘positive place for learning’. ​Our pupils benefit from our creative team of teachers and support staff. We are committed to excellent outcomes for all our pupils- including obtaining a Gold Healthy School Award for our wellbeing and sporting achievements.
Our motto is ‘Be the Best that you can be’ and Ofsted (2023) ​told us that ‘’ pupils behave maturely and leaders have high expectations that are commonly understood by all’. We aim to equip all our children with the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to be successful in their learning.
Parents and carers can meet with teachers at any time throughout the year. We have termly 1:1 meetings for parents, Informal Tea parties and fitness sessions for parents. We operate a free breakfast club for pupils from Reception to Y6 that offers a healthy breakfast and means that you can drop children off at 8am. We find this really helps pupils to have a calm start to the day, and aids concentration and learning. We also offer a Tea Time club until 4pm for our families – if you need an extra extension to the school day. Our After School Clubs provide an enriched offer that allow pupils to make friends and gain a variety of skills.
Our free Readiness Tuition and Booster offer for children ensures that no child is left behind. Our pupils all have access to online platforms that support their learning in school and our Reading Pledge ensures a love of reading for all pupils.
John Scurr himself believed strongly in fairness and equality and in the importance of developing a supportive community. Our current learning community continue with his tradition and we foster and develop his values through our mutual code of Respect, Resilience, Resourcefulness, Readiness and Reflection. ​By joining us you will also be part of creating that friendly atmosphere at our school.
Please do arrange to come and visit.

Computing
Our Curriculum Intent is for pupils to learn more, do more and know more.
Vision Statement:
Technology gives the quietest student a voice
What Do We Teach?
The key strands in our computing curriculum are:
All year groups are taught one computing lesson per week by our computing specialist teacher, Jack Fernie. This is taught as part of the PPA offer at John Scurr.
We follow the Teach Computing curriculum from the National Centre for Computing Education (NCCE). The curriculum is inclusive and ambitious. Where appropriate, activities are scaffolded so that all pupils can succeed and thrive. Scaffolded activities provide pupils with extra resources, such as visual prompts, to reach the same learning goals as the rest of the class. Exploratory tasks foster a deeper understanding of a concept, encouraging pupils to apply their learning in different contexts and make connections with other learning experiences.
Autumn 1: Computing systems and networks
Autumn 2: Creating media (A)
Spring 1: Programming (A)
Spring 2: Data and information
Summer 1: Creating media (B)
Summer 2: Programming (B)
How Do Pupils Learn?
We follow the pedagogical approach from the NCCE, which consists of 12 key principles underpinned by research:
The majority of assessment is done formatively, during lessons. Children complete e-books to chart their progress through a unit. We also use quizzes for summative assessment of children’s understanding of a topic.
Lead with concepts
Work together
Get hands on
Unplug, unpack, repack
Model everything
Foster program comprehension
Create projects
Add variety
Challenge misconceptions
Make concrete
Structure lessons
Read and explore code first
How Does The Curriculum Progress?
Progression within the computing curriculum is cumulative, meaning children build on their prior knowledge each year. Every year group learns through units within the same four themes, meaning their understanding of programming, for example, gets more complex as they get older. This progression is evidenced in each student’s e-book, which travels with them as they move up the school. Finally, each lesson within a unit is sequenced so that it builds on the learning from the previous lesson.
Celebrating Technology
Talented and enthusiastic students have the opportunity to join our after-school coding club, also run by Jack. Additionally, we are run termly ‘Tech challenges’, where students across the school can enter a technology-themed competition, with a judging process and prizes for the best entries. We want to encourage our talented computing students to aspire to be the best.

How do pupils learn
Students develop their ideas and skills in sketchbooks, using a variety of different materials and techniques every year. Each unit is supported by knowledge organisers which provide key artistic language and vocabulary students need to describe artworks and the process of art-making – informing both their own artistic practise and their critical thinking around key artists and artistic movements.
How does the curriculum progress
Each year children develop their skills and knowledge in drawing, painting, printmaking, textiles, 3D art and collage by revisiting prior techniques as well as increasing their exposure to new artists and ways of working. While this core content is revisited in all year groups, as children develop artistically, skills which are taught separately in Year 1 may be combined to allow children to explore mixed media ways of working in later years. For example, Year 1 pupils learn weaving skills and Year 3 pupils explore line and shape to make paper collages. This prior experience allows our Year 5 pupils to make informed artistic choices to create wall hangings with layered collage and weaving techniques. Key technical and tier 2 vocabulary is also mapped onto each unit, allowing children to build a rich bank of artistic language.
Links to learning
Artistic opportunities, when appropriate, are linked to curriculum learning and books students are reading in class. For example, observational contour drawing in Year 4 may be of Anglo-Saxon artefacts. Similarly, children are encouraged to read widely about the artists they are studying and have access to wider topic reading. Where suitable, children will also have opportunities to visit galleries or work alongside practising artists.
Social Development
At John Scurr School we participate in many other initiatives and activities to ensure all of our pupils receive a well-rounded, broad and balanced personal and social education.
You will see this not just within in our Edible Garden initiative and in our link with business partners from Canary Wharf but within our fundraising and Global learning projects.

Early Years Foundation Stage
Welcome to the EYFS
Every child deserves the best possible start in life and the support that enables them to fulfil their potential. Children develop quickly in the early years and a child’s experiences between birth and age five have a major impact on their future life chances.
"I like playing with all my friends. I play so many different things. I feel happy. I am learning to be happy all the time and I am learning everything about the whole wide world."
– Amelia Rahman, Reception.
Are you a new parent looking for an inspiring, creative and friendly nursery or Early Years place. Then please come and visit us, we are happy to answer any questions you may have.
Contact the school office 0207 790 3647 to arrange a suitable date and time.
The EYFS at John Scurr
At John Scurr Primary School, we endeavour to provide the best possible start for every child. We aspire for our children to become happy, confident and independent lifelong learners. We use a holistic approach to teaching and learning, building each child’s character, knowledge and understanding and skills. We take pride in building strong relationships with our children and their families. We ensure learning is exciting and engaging for our children, by providing a broad and balanced curriculum that will enable every child to progress and develop personally, emotionally, creatively and academically.
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) applies to children from birth to the end of the Reception year. At John Scurr Primary School, children join:
In partnership with parents and carers we enable the children to begin the process of becoming active learners for life.
This Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) Policy outlines the purpose, nature and organisation of the EYFS at John Scurr Primary School. The implementation of this policy is the responsibility of every practitioner working in the EYFS setting, and across the school.
Aims of the Early Years Foundation Stage
We believe that every child is entitled to the best possible start in their school life. This enables them to develop their full potential and be the best that they can be.
We aim to support each child’s welfare, learning and developmental needs by:
Providing opportunities to embed and review learning.

English
Vision Statement
​At John Scurr Primary School, English sits at the heart of our curriculum – it is through language, story and text that children learn to form concepts, connect ideas and express themselves. Through literacy, in all its forms, children learn to both make sense of our rapid and ever changing world and understand their place within it.
At our school, we believe that a strong foundation in vocabulary is essential for every child's success. From the age of two, our pupils embark on an exciting linguistic journey. We teach them to use key vocabulary and explore the fascinating connections between words through etymology and morphology. This comprehensive approach ensures that by the time they complete their primary education, they possess the language skills necessary to comprehend sophisticated texts and express themselves confidently in any situation. Our commitment to vocabulary development empowers our students to thrive academically and socially, setting them up for a bright future.
We have an ambitious, fulfilling and rewarding English curriculum that provides purposeful opportunities for speaking, reading and writing. Our English curriculum is taught, using CUSP (Curriculum by Unity Schools Partnership) from the very start of their journey in our two year old provision through to the end of their time at John Scurr in year six. This ensures that all children are seamlessly prepared for the next stage in their learning. The CUSP Curriculum has been deliberately designed using the latest evidence-based research.
Oracy
Speaking is at the heart of every learning experience. We believe that the quality and variety of language pupils hear and speak are vital for developing their vocabulary, grammar, and understanding of reading and writing. By continually fostering pupils’ confidence and competence in spoken language and listening skills, we equip them to lead successful, fulfilling lives.
Oracy is integrated across our curriculum using a structured framework. We teach children to respectfully discuss and explain their understanding using specific Oracy talk roles: launcher, builder, challenger, clarifier, prober, and summariser. Each classroom features a set of discussion guidelines that facilitate rich conversations and provide children with the confidence to share their ideas. We collaborate with Voice 21, CUSP Unity Curriculum and the Tower Hamlets Oracy Hub to embed Oracy skills throughout our curriculum.
"We believe all children, regardless of their background, are entitled to an Oracy education." - Voice 21
Oracy Assemblies
Weekly Oracy assemblies offer children the chance to debate and share their ideas with peers from different year groups. These assemblies involve mixed year groups seated in talking circles, discussing stimuli ranging from pictures and videos to stories and open-ended questions. Children lead the discussions, playing an active role in the assemblies.
Oracy Enrichment Opportunities
As a Lead CUSP School, we have been invited to participate in the first ever Festival of Spoken Word in November 2024. This will be an exciting opportunity for all children from year one to year six to refine and develop their spoken language, listening and presenting skills.
For our Year 5 and 6 students, we provide additional opportunities to develop presentational speaking and debating skills via Debate Mate, an extra-curricular club. Participants proudly represent the school in borough-wide debating competitions, including the Urban Debate League and the Debate Mate Cup. Add a hyperlink to the Debate Mate Club
At John Scurr Primary School, we are dedicated to nurturing articulate and confident communicators, prepared to thrive in a diverse and dynamic world.

Geography
‘You can travel the seas, poles and deserts and see nothing. To really understand the world, you need to get under the skin of the people and places. In other words, learn about geography. I can’t imagine a subject more relevant in schools.’
At John Scurr, our geography curriculum gives children the knowledge and skills to make sense of the world around them. It ensures they leave us with a secure understanding of where places are found, what they are like and the relationships between people and their environments. Our geography curriculum inspires curiosity in our children, encouraging them to find out more about the people and places in our world.

History
‘A people without the knowledge of their past history, origin and culture is like a tree without roots’
At John Scurr, our robust history curriculum ensures that pupils leave us with a secure understanding of our world today and the people and events who have shaped it across place and time. This supports them in understanding their own place in the world today, and in the long history of human development. Human societies are and always have been extremely complex and diverse. Our history curriculum at John Scurr helps pupils to appreciate these complexities and to celebrate the diversity of our world today and in the past.
We teach history at John Scurr, using the CUSP curriculum, which is structured around the principles of advancing both substantive and disciplinary knowledge cumulatively. We ensure that substantive knowledge is built upon cumulatively by centering our curriculum around 6 key substantive concepts: community, knowledge, invasion, civilisation, power and democracy. These concepts are the golden thread that run through our history curriculum from EYFS - Year 6, and are revisited and explored through different lenses year upon year. The effect of this cumulative model supports opportunities for children to associate and connect with significant periods of time, people, places and events
Disciplinary knowledge is also threaded through our history curriculum at John Scurr, giving our pupils an understanding of how historians investigate the past and construct historical claims. Our pupils therefore develop the tools to work historically and construct their own knowledge of the past. They go on to use this knowledge to investigate change, continuity, similarity, difference and significance within and across the periods of history studied.

Maths
“​Mathematics is not about numbers, equations, computations, or algorithms: it is about understanding..” William Paul Thurston
At John Scurr we provide the children with a rich and balanced mathematics curriculum that develops their fluency, reasoning and problem solving. We strive to ensure that all children achieve high standards in mathematics and develop confidence and positive attitudes to the subject. We intend the children to see mathematics as relevant in their daily lives and how their skills will support them in the future.
We plan, teach and assess to enable children to:
develop positive attitudes about mathematics
understand mathematical concepts deeply
recall and apply their knowledge rapidly
build on prior mathematical knowledge and understanding
find connections between mathematical ideas.
How Children Learn
At John Scurr, maths is taught using a mastery approach. Lessons are planned using high quality resources from White Rose and the NCETM. The Mastering Number programme is used in Reception and Key Stage 1. This ensures we have a well-constructed, progressive curriculum and maintains focus on children learning in small steps and exploring topics deeply. Lessons consist of opportunities for fluency, variation of representation and mathematical thinking. All children use manipulatives and pictorial representations to expose and make connections within concepts. At John Scurr, we emphasise the importance pupils’ oral contributions and ensure that all children can contribute. Mathematical vocabulary is displayed and modeled and key questions and sentence starters support and challenge learners.
Freckle, Numbots, Arithmagicians and Times Table Rockstars online programmes are used to support maths learning both in school and at home.
We offer a strong Professional Development offer to our staff including workgroups and training from the National Centre for Excellence in the Teaching of Mathematics (NCETM). We also offer professional development for a group of schools in the local area, supporting their teachers in the delivery of mathematics for mastery.
Cross-Curricular Links
Opportunities to practise, apply and develop mathematical understanding are provided across the curriculum. Opportunities are given to contextualize mathematical learning by linking it to the wider CUSP curriculum particularly within science, computing and design and technology.
Maths is celebrated across the school during National Numeracy week, where we celebrate mathematics in the world around us and have corporate visitors, who share their own maths stories. Mathematical enrichment aims to inspire children to be ambitious about their futures and helps them see how maths is applicable in all areas of their lives.
Support
Additional support is given to children who need it to enable them access the maths curriculum. Intervention groups are adapted to the needs of the children and may take place during maths lessons or in addition to them. We have access to additional online tutors, AI tutoring platforms as well as after school, small group readiness sessions led by teaching and support staff.
